messages.author: Tope
messages.message:
4) Most assets down in real terms.

I believe we are going to see the returns on capital to shrink in real terms. This applies to stocks, real estate and even some commodities.

It is likely that the hot AI stocks and the juiced up stocks (SPCX, PLTR, TSLA, etc) will suffer a significant correction in the next 18 months, which brings us to the next and final point:

messages.author: Tope
messages.message:
2) There is no path to victory in the middle east.

And I do mean, absolutly none.
From here, the only victory we can achieve is by moving the goal post.

Regime change in Iran from an aerial campaign is impossible.

No plausible path to open the Hormuz strait.

There is no secret winning strategy the US has been holding on to and is waiting for the right moment to deploy.

Best course of action is to bomb a few targets, claim victory (that no one will believe) and get out. Let Iran charge tolls.

messages.message:
Comparação direta para 30.000€
Imposto total (ordem de grandeza):

Portugal: ~8.500€ (SS + IRS)

Suécia: ~7.500–7.800€ (imposto sobre rendimento)

Líquido anual:

Portugal: ~21.500€

Suécia: ~22.200–22.500€

Taxa efetiva:

Portugal: ~28–29%

Suécia: ~23–26%

Se ajustarem isto à PPC vão ver que em PT os impostos singulares são inferiores aos suecos

messages.author: Hugo Condesa
messages.message:
Portugal não tem impostos altos ou baixos, baixar o IRC representaria um crescimento do PIB de 0,04%! (até se pode ver o impacto na madeira) o Interior paga de IRC menos de 450 milhões (todo o interior!!!), baixar o IRS não tem qualquer impacto no crescimento.
O problema são custos de contexto, legislaçãoetc- 

Comecemos por entender, porque a Suécia tem mais de 400 empresas cotadas! E lá chegaremos
